key_semantics.expected: What the plan expects when `go test ./...` runs at this tip commit. A proof owned by a landed slice is expected green. A proof owned by an unlanded slice is expected red.
key_semantics.honest: True when the test really calls the code and really asserts on the result, so its status means what it says. False for a planted stub, which is expected red by the plan but passes because it asserts nothing real.
key_semantics.style: Null for every honest test. For a planted stub, which of the three stub shapes it is: 'empty-body', 'commented-out' or 'always-true'.
key_semantics.where: For an honest red, the file and line of the assertion that fires. For an honest green, the file and line of the test function declaration. For a stub, the file and line of the stub itself: the declaration line of the empty body, the first commented out assertion line, or the always true condition line.
key_semantics.actual_status: Every honest proof matches its expected status. All three stubs are expected red and actually pass. That mismatch is the whole point of this repo.
